I farm conservatively, but I do not farm passively. I have 37 years in the field, I can irrigate from a well, and I have a small household with only 12 mu to manage, so I will keep the plan tight and labor-efficient. I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the backbone of my system and the most reliable use of my land. I will keep smaller areas in chili and cotton for diversification and cash income, but I will not spread myself too thin. Because I am educated and experienced, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it gives me more stable emergence, stronger stress tolerance, and better yield. I will fertilize wheat and maize more heavily than cotton and chili because they carry the main output of the farm, and with well irrigation I will water at the key growth stages rather than too often. I will use rotary tillage on most plots because it is efficient for my scale, but I will use plough tillage for cotton to improve rooting. I will control pests with a moderate number of sprays, enough to protect yield but not excessive. My goal this year is stable production first, then good cash return from the smaller cash-crop area.
